Q: Catching problem of multiple (non-equivalent) type definitions with the same name in C A:

To prevent this you need to define struct widget in helper.h

It doesn't need to be the truth.

#ifndef __HELPER_C__ 
struct widget { /* opaque */ };
#endif

result

In file included from caller.c:19:
./helper.h: At top level:
./helper.h:4:8: error: redefinition of ‘struct widget’
    4 | struct widget { /*opaque*/ };
      |        ^~~~~~
caller.c:3:8: note: originally defined here
    3 | struct widget1 {
      |        ^~~~~~

helper.c will now need

#define __HELPER_C__

Before the include.

Q: Is fetching std::chrono::steady_clock inside a critical section necessary to theoretically align C++ happens-before with real-time order? A:

You either have:

  • "clear", "empty" (the more natural case)
  • "ok", "clear" (the "inverted" execution)

Over a noticeable physical time gap (such as 1 hour), physical reality dictates t1 < t2.

Your timing seems huge, but you can also imagine a very slow machine with instructions which can take years to execute.

Waiting 1 year, 1h, 1s, 1ms is similar from the abstract machine.

And once you consider more "practical" cases, you are no longer in the theory.

Q: Roblox Lua: House generator stops running when math.random picks a duplicate number A:

The negative branch of your condition OldNum ~= RandomIndex does nothing: a new random value is generated, assigned to the local(!) variable RandomIndex, and is not used in any way. Moreover, even if it were used, there is no guarantee that it would not coincide with OldNum.

To ensure that you generate a number that is not equal to OldNum, you simply need to exclude it from the range:

local HouseModels = game.ReplicatedStorage.Houses:GetChildren()
local OldNum = math.random(#HouseModels) -- for 1st uniform distribution

function HouseGenerator.Generate(previousHouse)

    local r = math.random(#HouseModels - 1)
    local RandomIndex = (OldNum + r - 1) % #HouseModels + 1

    -- уour code is here

    OldNum = RandomIndex
    return CloneHouseModel
end
  1. math.random(#HouseModels - 1) generates r value in the range 1 .. #HouseModels-1.
  2. After adding OldNum, the result will always be greater than OldNum.
  3. Operation (OldNum + r - 1) % #HouseModels + 1 guarantees that the result will always be less than OldNum if OldNum + r exceeds #HouseModels.

This method has 3 advantages:

  • There are no branches or loops
  • It works when #HouseModels = 1
  • The time complexity is pure O(1)

Q: Can compiler ignore ill formed parts of the template body that are never used A:

When you instantited an object of the class by writing Foo<int> foo1;, only declarations of the member functions were instantiated. The definitions of the member function including the ctor Foo<T>::Foo(T) was never instntiated because of Foo<int> foo1; because you've not called(ord-used) that function. This means when you don't use the Foo<T>::Foo(T) ctor, the program is ill-formed no diagnostic required.

This can also be seen from:

The program is ill-formed, no diagnostic required, if:

  • 6.1) no valid specialization can be generated for a template or a substatement of a constexpr if statement within a template and the template is not instantiated, or

(emphasis mine)

If OTOH, you try to instantiate an object of this class template by using the parameterized ctor like say by writing Foo<int> foo2(1);, you'll note that all compilers will start rejecting the program. This is because, now by writing Foo<int> foo2(1);, you're actually using the ctor Foo<T>::Foo(T) and its definition will now be instantiated so this time the program will be ill-formed.

Q: How to write a general height-altering JavaScript function A:

id is expected to be unique as it is the unique identifier for an element. You can have multiple elements with same class name though. In that case, you can use

document.getElementsByClassName("class_name")[0].style.height = "200px";

document.getElementsByClassName("class_name") gives you an array of all elements with that class name in cronological order i.e. to access element with first occurance of that class you have to use 0th element as so on.

Note : never reuse an id.
